Gemini said

URL cloaking is a tech= nique used to disguise a long, complex, or unattractive web address (URL) i= nto a shorter, more user-friendly, or branded link. It is frequently used i= n affiliate marketing to hide tracking IDs and make links look more trustwo= rthy.

Depending on your technical comfort lev= el and where your website is hosted, there are several ways to achieve this= .

Method 1: Using a WordPress Plugin (Easies= t)

If your website runs on WordPress, you do= n't need to touch any code. Plugins handle the redirection and cloaking aut= omatically.

  • Popular Plugins:= Pretty Links<= /i> or ThirstyAffi= liates.

  • How it works:

    1. Install an= d activate the plugin.

    2. Go to= the plugin dashboard and click Add New Link.

    3. Paste your long destination URL (e.g., https://example.com/share?aff=3D12345&a= mp;source=3Dbio).

    4. Cre= ate your "cloaked" slug (e.g., mywebsite.com/recommend/product).

    5. Save the link. When users click your clean= link, they are seamlessly redirected to the destination.

Method 2: Using the .htaccess File (Apache Servers)

If you aren't using WordPress but your site r= uns on an Apache web server, you can cloak URLs by adding a redirect rule t= o your .htaccess file.

  1. Locate the .htaccess file in your website=E2=80=99s root directory u= sing an FTP client or your hosting file manager.

  2. Add a 301 (Permanent) or 302 (Temporary) redirect rule at the bottom of the file:

Apache
Redirect 302 =
/product-name https://example.com/share?aff=3D1=
2345
<= !---->=

  • Result: Anyone visitin= g yourwebsite.= com/product-name will be automatically forwarded to the long URL.

Method 3: Using a PHP Redirect File=

If you have a standard PHP-based website, = you can create a dedicated folder and file for the cloaked link.

  1. Creat= e a new folder on your server named after your desired slug (e.g., product).

  2. Inside that folder, create a file na= med index.php<= /code>.

  3. Paste the following cod= e into the file:

PHP
<?php
header("Location: https://example.com/share?aff=
=3D12345");
exit;
?>
<= !---->=

  • Result: When someone v= isits yourwebs= ite.com/product/, the server executes the PHP script and immediately= pushes them to the target URL.

M= ethod 4: HTML Meta Refresh (Simple but Slower)

If you can only edit basic HTML, you can use a meta refresh tag. This t= ells the user's browser to load a different URL after a set number of secon= ds.

  1. Create a blank HTML file (e.g., product.html).

  2. Add the following code:

=
HTML
= 
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <meta http-equiv=3D"refr=
esh" content=3D"0; url=3Dhttps://example.com/share?aff=3D12345">
    <title>=
Redirecting...</title>
</head>
<body>
    <p>If you are not redirected automatically, <a href=3D"https://example.com/share?aff=3D12345">=
;click here</a=
>.</=
p>
</body>
</html>
<= !---->=

Note: The = content=3D"0; tells the browser to redirect after 0 seconds. This me= thod is slightly slower than server-side methods (like PHP or .htaccess) because the = browser has to load the page first before redirecting.

Method 5: Using URL Shorteners

If you don't own a website or domain, you can use third-party URL short= ening services to cloak your links.

  • Services: Bitly, TinyURL, or Rebrandly.

  • How it works: You paste your = long URL into their generator, and they provide a shortened link (e.g., bit.ly/3xyz123). Some services allow you to use a custom domain for better branding.=

=E2=9A=A0=EF=B8=8F A Quick Best-Practice Note While URL cloaking is standard practice for branding and tracking clean-up,= avoid using it to deceive users or hide malicious destinations. Search eng= ines and ad networks (like Google Ads or Meta Ads) have strict policies aga= inst cloaking if it is used to show different content to ad reviewers than = what the final user actually sees. Always ensure your links lead exactly wh= ere the user expects them to go!

Best Practice for GitHub Pages Domains

If your goal is to map a custom domain that you ow= n directly to a GitHub Pages site so that the domain displays your GitHub c= ontent without changing the address bar, you should avoid HTML redirects. I= nstead:

  1. Go to your GitHub repository settings under Pages.

  2. Enter your custom domain in the Custom domain field.

  3. Configure the corresponding CNAME or A records within your DNS provide= r's dashboard (e.g., Cloudflare, Namecheap, or GoDaddy) pointing to GitHub'= s servers.

To load or disp= lay content from an external site (like a Cloudflare tunnel URL) inside a G= itHub Pages site, the standard web approach is to use an HTML <iframe> element.<= /p>

Here is how you can structure the HTML file t= o embed an external page:

HTML
<!DOCTYPE html>

    <meta charset=3D"UTF-8"<=

Embedded Site</title>

            margin: 0;
            padding: 0;

            width: 100%;

argeted-merchants-reduces-fails.trycloudflare.com"></iframe>

Important Technical Considerations

When attempting to embed external sites within GitHub = Pages via an iframe, you may run into two common web security restrictions:=

  • Mixed Content Restrictions:= GitHub Pages enforces HTTPS. If the target site or tunnel you are tryi= ng to embed does not use a valid, secure HTTPS connection, modern browsers = will block the iframe from loading to protect the user.

  • X-Frame-O= ptions / Content Security Policy (CSP): The server hosting the e= xternal site controls whether it can be embedded inside an iframe. If the t= arget server sends an X-Frame-Options: DENY or X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN HTTP header, = the browser will refuse to display the content inside your GitHub Pages sit= e, resulting in a blank space or an error message. If you control the desti= nation server or tunnel configuration, you must ensure its headers permit e= mbedding from your GitHub Pages domain.
